A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EGFN work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Original experiments and analyses can be matched across relocation and renumbering. Internal inconsistencies in v2 limit particular interpretations but do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original hypergrid, sEH, TFBind8, and QM9 experiments, including mode discovery, distribution errors, and component and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds antibody experiments, expanded comparisons and ablations, runtime measurements, and reward-evaluation analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 adds optional periodic replacement of the least-fit population member with star-agent parameters. Algorithm 1 also replaces a separate star-agent evaluation with storing its online training batch in replay. The underlying evolutionary search, replay mixing, and gradient training pipeline remains unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds antibody instability-index optimization, described as generating 50-residue sequences using an OAS antibody pair, and hu4D5 CDR H3 binder generation. These expand coverage to new protein-sequence populations and objectives. Hypergrid, sEH, TFBind8, and QM9 remain; the latter two move to Appendix D.

E2.justification: Hypergrid comparisons add GAFN, IQL, and GFN with random policy ensembles to v1's GFN/PPO/SAC/MARS comparisons. PPO's reward-sparsity curve disappears from v2 Figure 4, although its caption still names PPO. Figure 5 adds replay-buffer controls, and Figure 6 plots LED-GFN in the new antibody comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4 changes the stated population default from 10 to 5 and specifies doubled on-policy samples for PPO. However, v2 Appendix F.1 still states a default of 10, leaving the actual population setting unresolved. New antibody protocols introduce stability/binding thresholds and post-training evaluation of 1,000 samples with top-100 diversity and stability metrics; Appendix H adds reward-call-based evaluation.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and four hyperparameter studies, v2 adds a no-crossover control and additional replay controls in Figure 5, priority-percentile and priority-split sweeps in Appendix F.5–F.6, runtime analysis, reward-call efficiency comparisons, and population-versus-star-agent analysis. These substantially expand tests of mechanism, sensitivity, and computational cost.

E5.justification: Both versions specify means and variances over three random seeds for result figures. v2 adds uncertainty values for new timing results but does not specify increased repetitions, a different uncertainty-estimation procedure, or new significance testing.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for antibody tasks, comparator and ablation curves, and computational cost. New Table 1 reports EGFN versus GFlowNet edit distances of 40.47 versus 34.91 and instability indices of 35.95 versus 39.04. Revised hypergrid curves are not established same-setting improvements given the setting discrepancies. Relocated TFBind8, QM9, objective-comparison, and original sensitivity plots retain their results.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 corrects the flow-matching formulation from an expression using transition probabilities to incoming/outgoing estimated edge flows. It adds a normalized trajectory-flow definition and revises the trajectory-product bound in Equation 1. These are limited mathematical corrections and additions; neither version provides new EGFN theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claim that evolutionary sampling augments existing GFlowNet objectives and improves training under long trajectories and sparse rewards. The new contribution bullets summarize existing aims, while expanded experiments provide additional support without materially redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges that EGFN does not supply a new credit-assignment solution, adds approximately 35% runtime overhead in the reported QM9 comparison, and does not strictly equalize reward calls. It also changes the trajectory-length explanation from tending toward the mean to claimed uniformity and adds interpretations of priority sampling and population performance.

D1.justification: v2 adds antibody suffix sequences, discriminator architecture details, GAFN tuning values, hardware and runtime configurations, and crossover pseudocode. Algorithm 2 now includes the fitness accumulation already described in v1's prose. The stated implementation access changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. These materially expand reproducibility information, although setting inconsistencies remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting antibody scoring and datasets, IQL, crossover, and related sequence-generation methods, including Guruprasad, Mason, Kostrikov, Spears, Frey, and Ikram. Appendix E.2 adds a claimed distinction about unusually long trajectories. The main related-work discussion remains largely unchanged; publication updates and duplicate-citation consolidation do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: The evaluation narrative is reorganized around antibody tasks, with objective comparisons, TFBind8, and QM9 moved into Appendix D. v2 restructures the appendices, expands the discussion into limitations, revises the preliminaries, and adds contribution bullets, baseline descriptions, and ablation takeaways. This is substantial reorganization despite considerable retained prose.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a two-column conference layout to a predominantly single-column journal layout. Existing figures are relocated and resized; hypergrid plots receive revised legends and panel layouts. New antibody, priority-sampling, and analysis figures, two new result tables, and boxed takeaways substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct GAFN/random-ensemble comparisons and assessed efficiency mainly through training steps. v2 adds controls, reward-call comparisons, runtime measurements, and explicit limitations that substantially improve assessment of why EGFN helps and what it costs. Mathematical and algorithm-documentation corrections also help. Conflicting population defaults and an antibody reward formula that increases with the instability index being minimized weaken parts of the new evidence, but do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and transparency.
